### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the six activities A22, A20, A23, A24, A26 and A25 formed a rigid chain between A31 and A32: essentially all observed outgoing transitions of A31 went to A22, of A22 to A20 (about 99 in 100), of A20 to A23 (about 99 in 100), of A23 to A24 (all), of A24 to A26 (about 99 in 100), of A26 to A25 (about 99 in 100) and of A25 to A32 (about 93 in 100), and every activity pair kept one fixed distance of one to five steps. In the later window these successors redistributed — about 47 in 100 of A31's outgoing transitions now go to A24, A23 leads to A32 in about 49 in 100, and A25 reaches A32 in only about 43 in 100 — and the fixed distances spread across one to five steps. [DIR007, DIR002, DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG006, LAG016, LAG023, LAG024, LAG027]
- Pairs that previously had a single order now occur in both orders or reversed: A23 before A24 fell from about 99 in 100 traces to 15 in 100 (A24 before A23 now 83 in 100), A20 before A24 from 98 to 25 in 100, A23 before A26 from 99 to 32 in 100, while A23/A25, A20/A26 and A22/A24 are now mixed (about 48/52, 49/51 and 53/47). Both activities of every pair still co-occur in all traces in both windows. [REL006, REL001, REL008, REL007, REL003, REL004]
- Reversed orders that were almost unobserved earlier (about 1 in 200 traces) are now common: A24 before A20 within five steps occurs in about 148 of 200 later traces, A24 before A22 in about 94, and A26 before A20 in about 101. [LAG014, LAG015, LAG021]
- Positions moved consistently: in the later window A24 appears earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.65 to 0.59), while A23 (0.62 to 0.68) and A20 (0.59 to 0.63) appear later, and A26 and A25 slightly earlier. [POS004, POS003, POS001, POS006, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The 49 qualifying control-flow items are far above the roughly 0.66 expected by chance among the 132 tested units, so the pattern as a whole is not what an unchanged process typically produces. The evidence supports the hypothesis that the fixed sequential ordering of the block A22, A20, A23, A24, A26, A25 between A31 and A32 was relaxed in the later window: A24, which previously ran after A20 and A23, now typically executes earlier — often directly after A31 or A22 and before A20 and A23 — while A23, which previously preceded A24, A26 and A25, now typically executes later, near A32; pairs such as A23/A25, A20/A26 and A22/A24 lost their fixed order and now occur in both orders. The order reversals show this directly, the opposite position shifts of A24 (earlier) and A23 and A20 (later) agree with it, and the redistributed successors of A31, A23 and A25 and the spreading of the fixed distances fit the same picture. Participation itself did not change — every block activity still occurs in every trace in both windows — so this is a change in ordering constraints, not activities being added, removed or taken with different frequencies. [REL006, REL001, REL007, REL003, POS004, POS003, POS001, DIR007, DIR003, LAG016, LAG023]

Other differences: none beyond this reordering; the remaining direction and lag items involve the same activities and match the same pattern. [DIR006, LAG013, LAG018, LAG005]

Limitations: the items largely describe one underlying reordering rather than independent changes, and the evidence cannot distinguish a genuinely flexible order from a new fixed sequence with A23 and A24 exchanged, because some pairs keep a clearly dominant order in the later window (A24 before A23 in about 83 in 100 traces); a mixture of traces keeping the old order and traces following a new order is also compatible with the mixed shares. [REL006] A few lag items rest on about one earlier-window observation and are weak on their own. [LAG015, LAG019]
